newsitem.title: GREECE: Short-end of Greek yield curve up, bonds down.
newsitem.headline: Short-end of Greek yield curve up, bonds down.

text.p: The drachma gained ground against the ecu, trading below 311, after the central bank's intervention at the fixing and bonds were weaker on slightly higher short-term interbank rates, traders said.
"The overnight rate ended higher pulling the short-end of the yield curve up," said a dealer at a private bank. "This has definitely to do with a reduced supply of overnight funds."
The trader said the market was awaiting to see what the central bank will do in its regular depo tender of 14-day funds on Wednesday.
Fixed coupon bonds continued to be under light selling pressure with yields firming another five basis points and FRNs were trading marginally lower, dealers said.
They blamed the drift in bonds on a higher cost of funding in the interbank market and warned of greater pressure ahead if the Bank of Greece did not boost liquidity.
The mark was quoted at 159.34/39 from Tuesday's 159.400 fix, the dollar at 275.11/21 drachmas from 275.160 and the ecu at 310.75/85 from 310.990 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma has been drifting lower after the fixing," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "It is currently around 310.75/85."
Bank of Greece sold $30 million, 60 million ecus and 45 million marks for drachmas at the fixing on Tuesday.
